x-wolf-operation-semantics.acceptance: Associate the actual index-series job and save its admission result before background handoff. Busy/conflicting requests retain existing rejection semantics. Update terminal state only from the exact linked job.
x-wolf-operation-semantics.client: Persist public unknown identity before dispatch; cancellation is not server cancellation; poll lookup read only, never repeat POST. After refresh/reconnect/new instance keep uncertainty and separate latest business status.
x-wolf-operation-semantics.lookup: GET lookup is itself bound to current process; query fields name the original identity. Different original instance/config, missing/incomplete row ->200 state unknown. This is not proof of nonexecution. No business DB lookup for this endpoint.
x-wolf-operation-semantics.post_replay: Return saved initial status/body including recorded business rejection. Prior request not definitively associated after internal failure remains unknown; do not rerun it. Request IDs are not idempotency across process restart.
x-wolf-operation-semantics.retention: All association rows including final/rejected retained until process exit; no eviction. Existing identity lookup occurs before new-capacity check; new full request503 before business I/O. Reserve under process mutex after all guards and before acquiring business locks.
x-wolf-operation-semantics.state_constraints: Operation kind chooses matching business_status schema; job_id must equal status.job_id. accepted/running require nonnull job/reused_job/status and null rejection; completed/failed/interrupted require exact job terminal status and null rejection; rejected requires nonnull rejection, null job/status/reused_job; unknown has null status/rejection and nullable known job/reused_job. All combinations require explicit semantic tests.
x-wolf-operation-semantics.uniqueness: Within instance/config, reusing request_id for different operation or canonical body ->409 request_id_conflict, no second business call. Identical duplicate waits for original admission to settle or transport times out; it never repeats execution. Process mutex/row event released before background work.

x-wolf-transport.actual: Host then Origin/Fetch Metadata then marker, route/method, input/media/write switch, then bound context, then operation reservation/business I/O. Missing context ->400 connection_context_required; malformed ->400 connection_context_invalid; unequal frozen instance/config ->409 connection_context_mismatch. Missing marker ->403 client_marker_required.
x-wolf-transport.bind: 127.0.0.1 only; one worker; no reload/fork workers
x-wolf-transport.cache: All non-preflight API responses Cache-Control:no-store; no cache reuse across process/config. No redirect following by Client or proxy.

cors.error_headers: For an allowed Origin, all app responses including 4xx/500 carry CORS and Vary. Denied Origin gets no ACAO. Proxy neither invents Origin nor marker; reject/strip untrusted forwarding semantics.

x-wolf-transport.duplicate_headers: Reject duplicate raw header fields before joining/coercion (case insensitive names), including identical duplicates. Reject comma-joined singleton values and control/non-ASCII values. Exception: the single raw Access-Control-Request-Headers field is a comma-delimited set per preflight; normal multiple members are allowed, duplicate or unpermitted members rejected. HTTP parser rejections/connection-close occur before app and need raw transport evidence; no promise of JSON for parser failures.
x-wolf-transport.fallback: After global Host/Origin/metadata/marker guards: disabled/unknown route404 route_not_found; known route unsupported method405 method_not_allowed plus Allow containing its explicit methods and OPTIONS. No API HEAD supported in target; HEAD error has no body, its GET-equivalent error status/headers only. OPTIONS uses separate preflight guards and never requires actual marker. TRACE/CONNECT denied, no redirect or slash normalization creating bypass. Raw parser failures separately recorded.

400.description: Global fallback response

403.description: Global fallback response

404.description: Global fallback response

405.description: Global fallback response

x-wolf-transport.fetch_metadata: Without Origin reject Sec-Fetch-Site cross-site or same-site. With exact allowed Origin permit cross-site for explicitly allowed host pair; absent metadata is not proof of trust. Reject unknown/malformed metadata. Navigation mode or document/iframe/frame destination denied on actual API calls. Preflight evaluates Origin/method/headers only after Host.
x-wolf-transport.health: Public non-business diagnostic with common marker/Host/Origin guards; no context binding, no data-root probe. Storage field identifies configured backend kind, not disk readiness.
x-wolf-transport.host: Exactly one raw Host, exact configured 127.0.0.1:port. No localhost, IPv6, trailing dot, credentials or forwarded-host substitution. Proxy validates its own exact inbound authority and rewrites outbound Host only to its fixed backend authority.
x-wolf-transport.html: C1-02 actual HTML provider: enforced CSP frame-ancestors none (quoted none in header) and X-Frame-Options DENY on home, direct route and SPA fallback, both development/daily and final proxy response. This API contract does not generate or verify HTML headers.
x-wolf-transport.origin: Present Origin must be one exact configured entry; empty, null, wildcard, suffix match and unknown denied. This browser-read profile accepts only explicit http://127.0.0.1:port browser origins. Native schemes and implicit localhost:1420 are not enabled.
x-wolf-transport.post: Allowed nonmissing Origin; application/json optionally charset=utf-8; exact empty object; required request_id and bound context. Other media ->415; malformed JSON/invalid input ->422 invalid_request; no automatic retry. Extra JSON fields denied; unknown/duplicate query fields denied on every operation.
x-wolf-transport.preflight: Only known active path and supported advertised method. Require singleton Origin, requested method and requested-headers set including x-wolf-client, bound context names for business routes and request-id/content-type for writes. Set must be subset of allowed headers; order/case irrelevant, repeated names denied. No actual marker/context values, no writeswitch/context comparison or business I/O. Missing/invalid metadata400; denied Origin403; unknown path404; unsupported advertised method405.
